main_text.l: de oritur putredo. Sed Solis calor per se
semper uitalis est, & rerum omnium pro-
creandarum author, quemadmodum nos
docet philosophus libro de Generatione
& Corruptione secundo. Cum praeterea
Fernelius libro de Febribus, capite decimo
septimo, pestilentis febris causam esse per-
niciem, uenenatamq; qualitate e sublimi,
coelitusque in aerem demissam, tum nihil
probabile profert. Nam si e coelo uenenata
qualitas in aerem demitteretur duo insi-
gnia consequeretur absurda, quorum prius
esset, coelum uenenata qualitate esse prae-
ditum: alterum nempe accidens sine suo
proprioq; subiecto posse per se loco dimo-
ueri. Atqui coelum nec uenenatum est, ne-
que ulla qualitas per se loco moueri po-
test[?]. Propterea pestilentis febris causa ex-
terna non est aeris qualitas, quae e coelo
promanet, sed potius ex cadauerum mini-
mè crematorū, sepulcrorumue, aut lacuum
ac paludum euaporatione, quemad-
modum nobis ostendit Gale-
nus libro de Differen-
tijs Febrium
primo.

page.notes: The word "poterit" or "potest" at the end of the line "neque ulla qualitas per se loco moueri po-reft" is doubtful; marked [?]. The "Cap.9." marginal mark is partly rendered in the scan and is read as "Cap.9.". After "primo." a small printed mark (a reference or printer's sign) follows; it is not transcribed. Line 7 of the text: "caufam" and "qualitate" are clear in the scan but show some ink damage. Word "quorum" and "esset" are somewhat blurred. The short underlined mark after "primo." is a printer's mark and is not copied as text.
